EXSC 110.description: Focusing on the mind-body-spirit connection, individuals assume responsibility for their health through everyday choices. Students learn about and expand on the pillars of holistic health.
EXSC 110.subject: EXSC
EXSC 110.title: Holistic Health and Fitness

EXSC 110L.description: Lab focusing on how to implement and practice techniques that promote health and well-being through the holistic practices.
EXSC 110L.subject: EXSC
EXSC 110L.title: Holistic Health and Fitness Lab

EXSC 191.description: Concepts of exercise, nutrition, behavior changes, and skills to promote lifelong physical activity and health.
EXSC 191.subject: EXSC
EXSC 191.title: Physical Activity and Health

EXSC 200.description: Examination of careers and specific practices within sports medicine, specifically athletic training.
EXSC 200.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 223 and EXSC 223L.
EXSC 200.subject: EXSC
EXSC 200.title: Introduction to Sports Medicine and Athletic Training

EXSC 201.description: Introduction to the profession and practice of physical therapy detailing the functions, disorders, and therapies of the major organ systems in applied context.
EXSC 201.subject: EXSC
EXSC 201.title: Foundations of Physical Therapy

EXSC 210.description: Students enrolled in this course will discuss and learn how to apply evidence-based learning strategies that will increase the likelihood of success in the pursuit of a college degree.
EXSC 210.subject: EXSC
EXSC 210.title: Effective Learning Strategies

EXSC 223.description: The structure and functions of the human body: tissues, integument, skeletal, muscular, respiratory, and reproductive systems, and regulation of eating and metabolism.
EXSC 223.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 102; BIOL 102; CHEM 111; MATH 122 or MATH 141.
EXSC 223.subject: EXSC
EXSC 223.title: Anatomy and Physiology I

EXSC 223L.description: Hands-on activities covering micro- and macroscopic anatomical topics including identification of tissues, bones and markings of the skeletal system, the joints, and the skeletal muscles of the body.
EXSC 223L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 102; BIOL 102, CHEM 111; MATH 122 or MATH 141.
EXSC 223L.subject: EXSC
EXSC 223L.title: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory

EXSC 224.description: The structure and functions of the human body: nervous, cardiovascular, digestive, immune, urinary, and endocrine systems.
EXSC 224.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 223 and EXSC 223L.
EXSC 224.subject: EXSC
EXSC 224.title: Anatomy and Physiology II

EXSC 224L.description: Hands-on activities covering the gross anatomy nervous, cardiovascular, digestive, and muscular systems.
EXSC 224L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in both EXSC 223 and EXSC 223L.
EXSC 224L.subject: EXSC
EXSC 224L.title: Anatomy and Physiology II Lab

EXSC 275.description: Human anatomy for allied health professions. Focus on anatomy relevant to providing health services; knowledge and skills of orthopedic anatomy relative to muscle, ligament, and tendon; muscle origins, insertions, innervations, and actions pertaining to joint motion.
EXSC 275.subject: EXSC
EXSC 275.title: Functional Musculoskeletal Anatomy

EXSC 275L.description: Clinical application of human anatomy for allied health care professions using discussion, models, and charts. Anatomy relevant to providing health care to individuals.
EXSC 275L.subject: EXSC
EXSC 275L.title: Functional Musculoskeletal Anatomy Lab

EXSC 303.description: Theoretical foundations and observation of growth and motor development of children, age birth to 10 years. Observation will be provided via video and live subjects provided by the instructor.
EXSC 303.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in both EXSC 224 and EXSC 224L.
EXSC 303.subject: EXSC
EXSC 303.title: Perceptual-Motor Development

EXSC 330.description: The individual and combined roles of the major organ systems of the body in maintaining homeostasis during muscular exercise.
EXSC 330.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 224 and EXSC 224L.
EXSC 330.subject: EXSC
EXSC 330.title: Exercise Physiology

EXSC 330L.description: Laboratory procedures in exercise physiology; measurement of physical fitness components.
EXSC 330L.subject: EXSC
EXSC 330L.title: Exercise Physiology Lab

EXSC 335.description: Kinetic and kinematic principles governing efficient human movement. Selected methods of analyzing human movement will be reviewed.
EXSC 335.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 224, EXSC 224L, PHYS 201 and PHYS 201L.
EXSC 335.subject: EXSC
EXSC 335.title: Biomechanics of Human Movement

EXSC 341A.description: First hour of a supervised practicum in a clinical setting for the Health Fitness Track.
EXSC 341A.subject: EXSC
EXSC 341A.title: Health Fitness Practicum

EXSC 351.description: Scientific and behavioral foundation of the learning and performance of motor skills.
EXSC 351.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in EXSC 224 and EXSC 224L.
EXSC 351.subject: EXSC
EXSC 351.title: Acquisition of Motor Skills

EXSC 355.description: Novel and emerging themes in exercise science. Content varies by instructor and title. May be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours as content varies by title.
EXSC 355.subject: EXSC
EXSC 355.title: Special Topics in Exercise Science

EXSC 395.description: The research process in exercise science; participation in, presentation and discussion of current research.
EXSC 395.subject: EXSC
EXSC 395.title: Research Seminar in Exercise Science

EXSC 401.description: Integration of major program of study and general education; issues of transition into senior practicum - EXSC 444 .
EXSC 401.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330.
EXSC 401.subject: EXSC
EXSC 401.title: Practicum Preparation

EXSC 407.description: Introduction to the large scientific and philosophical literature base related to bull, with a focus on the occurrence of bull in exercise science. Defining, identifying, and refuting bull when it is encountered in scientific literature, the news, social media, and casual conversation.
EXSC 407.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330 and EXSC 330L; C or better in STAT 201 or STAT 205.
EXSC 407.subject: EXSC
EXSC 407.title: Calling Bull in the Age of Big Data, Social Media, and False Claims

EXSC 410.description: Introduction to psychosocial factors in physical activity. Topics include mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to physical activity, and physical activity determinants and interventions.
EXSC 410.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101.
EXSC 410.subject: EXSC
EXSC 410.title: Psychology of Physical Activity

EXSC 444.description: Supervised experience in a field, clinical, or research setting. EXSC majors only.
EXSC 444.subject: EXSC
EXSC 444.title: Exercise Science Practicum

EXSC 454.description: Design and implementation of health/fitness programs.
EXSC 454.subject: EXSC
EXSC 454.title: Health/Fitness Programs

EXSC 464.description: Performance of pre-exercise assessments, development of appropriate exercise training programs based on these assessments, and development and conduct of safe and effective methods of exercise by the application of the primary theories and principles of exercise science.
EXSC 464.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in both EXSC 224 and EXSC 224L.
EXSC 464.subject: EXSC
EXSC 464.title: Conditioning Methods in Athletic Performance

EXSC 465.description: The art of exercise testing and prescription for athletes, general and special populations through classroom and hands on experience.
EXSC 465.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330 and EXSC 330L.
EXSC 465.subject: EXSC
EXSC 465.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription

EXSC 499.description: Enrollment and topic to be approved in advance by advisor and instructor.
EXSC 499.subject: EXSC
EXSC 499.title: Independent Study

EXSC 507.description: The relationship between exercise, sport performance, and nutrient metabolism.
EXSC 507.subject: EXSC
EXSC 507.title: Exercise, Sport, and Nutrition

EXSC 531.description: Scientific bases of clinical exercise programming. The fitness instructor’s role in encouraging changes in exercise behavior.
EXSC 531.subject: EXSC
EXSC 531.title: Clinical Exercise Physiology

EXSC 541.description: Investigation on the physiological basis for strength and conditioning. Principles of strength and conditioning through lecture based learning, demonstrations, and through laboratory activities.
EXSC 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330.
EXSC 541.subject: EXSC
EXSC 541.title: Physiological Basis for Strength and Conditioning

EXSC 555.description: Content varies by title. Course may be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours.
EXSC 555.subject: EXSC
EXSC 555.title: Current Topics in Exercise Science

EXSC 562.description: Role of motor development in the growth and development of individuals exhibiting impaired motor control.
EXSC 562.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: biology, anatomy, physiology, or the equivalent.
EXSC 562.subject: EXSC
EXSC 562.title: Impairments of the Human Motor System

EXSC 563.description: The effects of age and physical activity on physical and motor functions of elderly individuals.
EXSC 563.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: EXSC 223, EXSC 224, EXSC 351, EXSC 330, EXSC 330L.
EXSC 563.subject: EXSC
EXSC 563.title: Physical Activity and the Physical Dimensions of Aging

EXSC 585.description: Sex differences in diseases, physiological function of sex hormones, hormonal changes in a woman’s life, specific women’s health issues, and role of physical activity and exercise in prevention and treatment of conditions and diseases specific to women or related to sex hormones. Restricted to 30 students, Special Permission by Instructor.
EXSC 585.subject: EXSC
EXSC 585.title: Women’s Health and Physical Activity

EXSC 608.description: The course will increase students’ understanding of the theoretical foundations, scientific evidence and practical application of technology-assisted lifestyle interventions, with an emphasis on behavioral weight control for adults.
EXSC 608.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 410.
EXSC 608.subject: EXSC
EXSC 608.title: Apps, Wearables and Technology for Lifestyle Behavior Change and Weight Loss

EXSC 610.description: Application of neuroscientific theories and measurements to human performance and expertise.
EXSC 610.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330, EXSC 330L, EXSC 351, and EXSC 410.
EXSC 610.subject: EXSC
EXSC 610.title: Neuroscience of Human Performance

EXSC 620.description: Examination of the interrelationships that link human nutrition to the immune system in health and disease. Topics will include basic immunology, overview of nutritional sources, deficiencies and excesses, and the impact on public health issues such as exercise, disease and aging.
EXSC 620.subject: EXSC
EXSC 620.title: Nutrition and Immunology

EXSC 641.description: The aim of this course is to acquire a fundamental understanding of how concepts from motor learning, neurophysiology, and muscle physiology are applied to functional strength training.
EXSC 641.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330, EXSC 330L, EXSC 351.
EXSC 641.subject: EXSC
EXSC 641.title: Neuromuscular Basis of Functional Strength Training

EXSC 651.description: Students in this course will analyze everyday activities to gain insight into how humans plan, initiate, execute and refine motor skills. Students will also learn how to evaluate research on motor behavior and how to create novel studies aimed at advancing our understanding of everyday motor behavior.
EXSC 651.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 351.
EXSC 651.subject: EXSC
EXSC 651.title: Analysis of Everyday Motor Behavior

EXSC 660.description: Physiological and psychosocial impact of cancer and its treatments on individuals, and how this impacts the design and delivery of exercise programs before, during and after cancer treatments.
EXSC 660.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330 and EXSC 330L.
EXSC 660.subject: EXSC
EXSC 660.title: Exercise Oncology

EXSC 663.description: This course is designed to provide students a survey of physiological responses to a variety of environments, such as heat, cold, altitude, and microgravity environments, and how the body acclimatizes to these environments with regards to exercise training.
EXSC 663.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330 and EXSC 330L.
EXSC 663.subject: EXSC
EXSC 663.title: Environmental Exercise Physiology

EXSC 666.description: Examination of the anatomy and function of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems of the exercising human organism, including acute adjustments and chronic adaptations to the systems.
EXSC 666.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 330.
EXSC 666.subject: EXSC
EXSC 666.title: Cardiorespiratory Exercise Physiology

EXSC 669.description: Skeletal muscle physiology and exercise through select laboratory experiences and discussion of related research literature.
EXSC 669.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in both EXSC 330 and EXSC 330L.
EXSC 669.subject: EXSC
EXSC 669.title: Skeletal Muscle Physiology: Form and Function

EXSC 690.description: A comprehensive overview of the methods and skills needed to design and interpret research including developing a research question, writing a research proposal, designing appropriate protocols to test the research question, conducting ethical research, and professional presentation and dissemination of research.
EXSC 690.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in EXSC 224 and EXSC 224L; C or better in STAT 201, STAT 205, or STAT 206.
EXSC 690.subject: EXSC
EXSC 690.title: Research Methods Design for the Exercise Sciences

EXSC 695.description: The research process in Exercise Science through participation, presentation, and discussion of current research.
EXSC 695.subject: EXSC
EXSC 695.title: Writing and Presenting in Research

EXSC 700.description: An introduction to exercise science with emphasis on the relationships between exercise and health for promotion of physical activity in clinical and public health settings.
EXSC 700.subject: EXSC
EXSC 700.title: Physical Activity and Health: Epidemiology, Research and Practice

EXSC 706.description: Assessment of infant, child, adolescent, and adult motor behavior.
EXSC 706.subject: EXSC
EXSC 706.title: Assessment of Motor Behavior

EXSC 710.description: Psychosocial and behavioral factors in physical activity. Topics include mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to physical activity, and physical activity determinants and interventions.
EXSC 710.subject: EXSC
EXSC 710.title: Behavioral Aspects of Physical Activity

EXSC 711.description: This course is designed to introduce students to Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) or Experience Sampling Methods (ESM) for health behavior research. EMA/ESM is a real-time data capture strategy that can be assisted by mobile technologies to assess behaviors, experiences, and exposures in real-world settings. This course will provide an overview of the EMA literature and introduce different EMA approaches and designs to collect data on individuals’ health determinant(s) and/or outcomes. The primary goal of the course is to enable students to apply course concepts and learned skills to develop and implement EMA/ESM in their fields of study.
EXSC 711.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Students should have an introductory understanding of research design and quantitative methods; for example, students are expected to complete at least one graduate-level statistics and methods course (examples: EXSC 787, HPEB 707, BIOS 700, BIOS 757, EDRM 711).
EXSC 711.subject: EXSC
EXSC 711.title: Ecological Momentary Assessment in Health Behavior Research

EXSC 723.description: The part lecture and part discussion course will explore genetic research in the health sciences, with emphasis on human genetic association studies, clinical utility for personalized medicine, direct-to-consumer genetic testing, and ethical issues. Students will receive hands-on experience searching, interpreting, and summarizing genetic studies on a topic of their choice.
EXSC 723.subject: EXSC
EXSC 723.title: Genetics in Health Sciences

EXSC 727.description: This course covers planning, organizing and implementing randomized controlled trials of physical activity or exercise interventions. It is primarily aimed to meet the needs of graduate students in exercise science and others in related fields.
EXSC 727.subject: EXSC
EXSC 727.title: Controlled Trials in Exercise Science

EXSC 731.description: A study of theories and mechanisms involved in human movement. Focus is on analysis of principles and systems of gross motor control and learning.
EXSC 731.subject: EXSC
EXSC 731.title: Mechanisms of Motor Skill Performance

EXSC 732.description: Overview of measurement theory and measures to assess body composition and associated health behaviors (i.e., physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep, diet).
EXSC 732.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOS 700, BIOS 701, or PUBH 725; for MPH-PAPH students, EXSC 700.
EXSC 732.subject: EXSC
EXSC 732.title: Measurement of Body Composition and Associated Health Behaviors

EXSC 735.description: This course focuses on fundamentals of biomechanics emphasizing measurement of human movement and motor control. Content presented is essential to understanding human movement, exercise training, movement impairment and injury. Utilization and interpretation of instrumentation for capturing, describing and quantifying human movement and motor control will be covered (e.g., electromyography, kinematics).
EXSC 735.subject: EXSC
EXSC 735.title: Applied Human Biomechanics

EXSC 742.description: Study of the procedures involved in screening and testing persons with varying levels of functional work capacity.
EXSC 742.subject: EXSC
EXSC 742.title: Clinical Exercise Testing

EXSC 754.description: Role of the physical activity specialist within the community health department. Development, initiation, and evaluation of campaigns, resources, community capacity building, and coalitions to promote physical activity.
EXSC 754.subject: EXSC
EXSC 754.title: Community-Based Physical Activity Interventions

EXSC 755.description: A study of selected issues in exercise science. Content varies by title.
EXSC 755.subject: EXSC
EXSC 755.title: Special Topics in Exercise Science

EXSC 775.description: Current and historical perspectives on the neural basis of skilled motor behavior.
EXSC 775.subject: EXSC
EXSC 775.title: Neural Basis of Skilled Motor Behavior

EXSC 776.description: Examine the current evidence related to popular nutritional and pharmacological ergogenic aids.
EXSC 776.subject: EXSC
EXSC 776.title: Ergogenic Aids: Science vs. Myth

EXSC 777.description: The course examines the endocrine system, its interaction with the nervous system, and how they affect human biology before, during, and after exercise. Special attention will be paid to this system’s influence on the relationship between physical activity and health.
EXSC 777.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: At least one undergraduate or graduate course in statistics and molecular or cellular biology.
EXSC 777.subject: EXSC
EXSC 777.title: Endocrinology of Exercise and Health

EXSC 778.description: Causes and treatment of childhood obesity with special reference to the role of exercise in prevention and early intervention.
EXSC 778.subject: EXSC
EXSC 778.title: Exercise and Childhood Obesity

EXSC 780.description: Physiological responses to exercise: skeletal muscle structure and function, cardiorespiratory function, physiological determinants of exercise performance, and training adaptations. Didactic and laboratory included.
EXSC 780.subject: EXSC
EXSC 780.title: Physiology of Exercise

EXSC 781.description: The input and response to exercise in diseased populations. Diseases to be examined include cardiovascular disease, age-related diseases, pulmonary, renal, and other conditions.
EXSC 781.subject: EXSC
EXSC 781.title: Physiology, Exercise, and Disease

EXSC 783.description: Presentation and discussion of current research topics in exercise physiology.
EXSC 783.subject: EXSC
EXSC 783.title: Research Seminar in Exercise Physiology

EXSC 784.description: Techniques used in exercise testing (including principles of electrocardiology) and in design and delivery of exercise programs for enhancing the health of normal and cardiopulmonary-diseased populations.
EXSC 784.subject: EXSC
EXSC 784.title: Cardiovascular/Pulmonary Testing and Programming

EXSC 787.description: The major goal of this course is to provide an in-depth examination of: research concepts, terminology, experimental, non-experimental, and epidemiological designs, internal and external validity, methods for establishing causality investigating associations, and application of designs to test hypotheses in research of exercise science-related outcomes.
EXSC 787.subject: EXSC
EXSC 787.title: Research Methods and Design for Exercise Science

EXSC 790.description: Topics to be assigned and approved by advisor, graduate director, and department head.
EXSC 790.subject: EXSC
EXSC 790.title: Independent Study

EXSC 795.description: Clinical practice in an applied area of exercise science. Requirements include at least 20 hours fieldwork per week with intensive supervision.
EXSC 795.subject: EXSC
EXSC 795.title: Internship in Exercise Science

EXSC 796.description: This course is designed to provide students with a culminating seminar focused on the synthesis of foundational and MPH-PAPH competencies in preparing a high quality grant proposal to address a public health problem.
EXSC 796.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PUBH 724, PUBH 725, PUBH 726, PUBH 730, and PUBH 735; B or better in EXSC 700, EXSC 710, and EXSC 780.
EXSC 796.subject: EXSC
EXSC 796.title: Physical Activity Integrative Learning Experience

EXSC 797.description: The focus of this course is the performance of a limited work or service project in an approved public need setting and the demonstration of at least 5 competencies related to previously identified aspects of the student’s chosen role.
EXSC 797.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PUBH 724, PUBH 725, PUBH 726, PUBH 730, and PUBH 735; B or better in EXSC 700, EXSC 710, and EXSC 780.
EXSC 797.subject: EXSC
EXSC 797.title: Physical Activity Applied Practice Experience

EXSC 798.description: Independently executed project designed to expand the student’s knowledge of exercise science.
EXSC 798.subject: EXSC
EXSC 798.title: Project in Exercise Science

EXSC 801.description: The course will provide an overview of ethical issues scientists encounter conducting and disseminating public health research. Topics include the history of ethics in public health, working with human participants, conflicts of interests, spin, and creating safe and healthy workplaces.
EXSC 801.subject: EXSC
EXSC 801.title: Ethical Conduct in Public Health Research

EXSC 802.description: The course is designed to enable predoctoral students to gain grant writing experience, develop into productive, independent research scientists, and to obtain mentored research training while conducting dissertation research.
EXSC 802.subject: EXSC
EXSC 802.title: Predoctoral Fellowship Writing Course with Special Emphasis on NIH F31

EXSC 805.description: The major goal for all students taking this course is to provide an overview of how to conduct systematic reviews and meta-analyses from published scientific literature. Emphasis is placed on developing a working knowledge of how to conceptualize a literature review, keyword search for relevant articles through online databases, define inclusion and exclusion criteria, develop coding schemes for study information, and the calculation of effect sizes using published data. For students taking more than 1-credit the additional goals are to provide hands-on experience in conducting a systematic review and meta-analysis, calculating effect sizes, and learning to use meta-analysis software.
EXSC 805.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOS 700 and BIOS 701 or their equivalent; C or better in BIOS 757 or equivalent is strongly recommended.
EXSC 805.subject: EXSC
EXSC 805.title: Introduction to Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis

EXSC 808.description: Examination of neural repair and rehabilitation from a clinical perspective.
EXSC 808.subject: EXSC
EXSC 808.title: Neuro Repair - Rehabilitation

EXSC 880.description: Study of muscle contraction mechanics, energetics, and metabolism and the relationship of these processes to physical training, athletics, and rehabilitation.
EXSC 880.subject: EXSC
EXSC 880.title: Myology and Exercise

EXSC 881.description: Study of mechanisms for cardiovascular and respiratory responses to acute exercise and adaptations to these systems with chronic physical activity.
EXSC 881.subject: EXSC
EXSC 881.title: Advanced Cardiorespiratory Exercise Physiology

EXSC 882.description: An examination of physical activity/exercise habit patterns as they relate to health status. Emphasis on the chronic effects of exercise.
EXSC 882.subject: EXSC
EXSC 882.title: Physical Activity and Health: Epidemiology and Research Methods
